group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: POLARIS
title: SoK: Private LLM Inference using Approximate Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Reference CKKS implementation combining the SoK's recommended model-preserving building blocks.
note: Open-source PoC reference framework; model-preserving, GPU accelerated; 0% accuracy loss on SST-2 subset.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: THOR
authors: Moon, Omarov, Yoo, Cho et al. (Desilo)
title: THOR: Secure transformer inference with homomorphic encryption
rel: Model-preserving CKKS evaluation of BERT-Base using normalize-and-square Softmax, Goldschmidt division and aSOR.
note: First model-preserving BERT-Base under CKKS; only 5-6 orders of magnitude slower than FP16 GPU cleartext.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: CEP / EncryptedLLM (GPU-accelerated FHE GPT-2)
title: EncryptedLLM: Privacy-Preserving Large Language Model Inference via GPU-Accelerated Fully Homomorphic Encryption
rel: First open GPU-accelerated CKKS bootstrapping backend for OpenFHE; model-preserving GPT-2 decoding.
note: ~150x speedup over CPU OpenFHE; adopts NEXUS arg max.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: CACHEMIR
authors: Yu, Zhou, Chen, Soto et al.
title: Cachemir: Fully Homomorphic Encrypted Inference of Generative Large Language Model with KV Cache
rel: Graph-based bootstrapping placement (extends Orion) and cyclic encodings for multi-head attention.
note: Model-preserving Llama-3-8B decoding with KV cache; about 4 orders of magnitude slower than cleartext.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: CERIUM
authors: Jayashankar, Kim, Sullivan, Zheng et al.
title: A scalable multi-GPU framework for encrypted large-model inference
rel: First end-to-end multi-GPU CKKS compiler with kernel fusion; ~14 KB ciphertext memory per model parameter.
note: Best-known runtimes for model-preserving Llama-3-8B; bootstrapping under 10 ms on multi-GPU cluster.
latency: 134 s prefill (128 tokens, 8x B200); 66 s BERT-Base on A100

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: SplitPrompt
authors: Park, Park, Park, Ahn et al.
title: Scaling up FHE-based Privacy-Preserving ML: Higher Throughput, Longer Inputs for LLama-3-8B (v1: Scaling up Privacy-Preserving ML: A CKKS Implementation of Llama-2-7B)
family: CKKS · Model-preserving, hybrid public-private prompt split (N-PRE†)
rel: Relaxed threat model: only sensitive tail of the prompt is encrypted, rest processed in the clear.
note: Normalize-and-square Softmax; Chebyshev SiLU; shows practicality of hybrid prompt partitioning.
latency: 33-34 s per output token; 85 s summarization with 4096 tokens (128 encrypted)

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: ARION
title: ARION: Attention-optimized transformer inference on encrypted data
rel: CPU-only Lattigo implementation with column/diagonal packing.
note: Strong amortized throughput on CPU; requires architectural modifications.
latency: 9.3 s (Tiny) / 225 s (Base) amortized per sequence, batch 256

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: ELLMO
authors: Guzelhan, Daksha, Agulló Domingo, Jonatan, Kim et al.
title: ELLMo: Packing- and Depth-Aware Encrypted Transformer Inference
rel: Pre-computed plaintext transforms to minimize depth; delayed LayerNorm; statistical max estimation.
note: Fastest BERT-Tiny entry in the SoK; sequence length not reported.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: RL (Rovida & Leporati)
title: Transformer-based language models and homomorphic encryption: An intersection with BERT-tiny
rel: Early open-source CKKS BERT-Tiny with precomputed LayerNorm statistics.
note: Educational baseline; accuracy loss >1.5% / retraining needed.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: TRICYCLE
title: TRICYCLE: Private transformer inference with tricyclic encodings
rel: Tricyclic encodings process multiple attention heads per ciphertext; statistical max for Softmax.
note: CPU-only; closed source.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: EFLA (Encryption-Friendly LLM Architecture)
authors: Rho, Kim, Lee et al. (CryptoLab / SNU)
title: Encryption-friendly LLM architecture
rel: Gaussian-kernel attention replaces Softmax; LoRA fine-tuning under CKKS.
note: Also addresses encrypted fine-tuning, not just inference.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: PRITRAN
title: PRITRAN: Privacy-preserving inference for transformer-based language models under FHE
rel: Row packing with precomputed LayerNorm statistics.
note: No utility metric reported.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: EUSTON
authors: Gao, Fu, Liu, Liu, Luo et al.
title: Euston: Efficient and User-Friendly Secure Transformer Inference with Non-Interactivity
rel: SVD/precomputed transforms to reduce depth; NEXUS arg max.
note: Scales to Llama-3-8B classification with modest accuracy loss.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: Powerformer
title: Powerformer: Efficient and high-accuracy privacy-preserving language model with homomorphic encryption
rel: Batch rectifier power max replaces Softmax; 90% reduction in Softmax cost.
note: Requires retraining/distillation.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: MOAI
authors: Zhang, Wang, Sim, Huang, Zhong, Wang
title: MOAI: Module-optimizing architecture for non-interactive secure transformer inference
rel: Bootstrapping inside Softmax before division halves required levels (20 to 10).
note: Depth-minimization placement; constant max values from plaintext profiling.
latency: 141 s BERT-Base amortized; 225 s Llama-3-8B decode (8 tokens)

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: NEXUS
title: Secure transformer inference made non-interactive
rel: Introduced O(log V) SIMD-folding QuickMax arg max adopted by CEP, MOAI, EUSTON.
note: First end-to-end non-interactive CKKS transformer; widely used baseline.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: STIP
authors: Wang, Chen, Gao, Wang, Liu et al.
title: STIP: Efficient and secure non-interactive transformer inference via compact packing
rel: Uses both real and imaginary slots; Gaussian-kernel attention; delayed LayerNorm.
note: Compact packing; model modifications required.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: ENSI
authors: He, Wang, Gao, Luo, Liu, Fu
title: ENSI: Efficient non-interactive secure inference for large language models
rel: BitNet ternary weights replace multiplications with additions; sigmoid attention.
note: Model-modifying; demonstrates 1.58-bit LLMs under FHE.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: Polyformer
title: Converting transformers to polynomial form for secure inference over homomorphic encryption
rel: 100% polynomial transformer via scaled-sigma attention and range-minimization training.
note: Requires retraining; HELayers tile tensors.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: SecretVoice 1.0
title: SecretVoice1.0: Non-interactive secure transformer inference
rel: Fuses linear layers into StC-first bootstrapping.
note: Operation fusion trades memory for latency; no utility metric.

group: 0. CKKS LLM frameworks surveyed in the SoK
name: RZW (encrypted LoRA split model)
title: Practical secure inference algorithm for a fine-tuned large language model based on fully homomorphic encryption
interaction: non-interactive FHE on LoRA modules only
rel: Only encrypted LoRA adapters are evaluated server-side; base model runs at client in the clear.
note: Protects proprietary fine-tuning rather than full prompt privacy.

name: CKKS (HEAAN)
title: Homomorphic Encryption for Arithmetic of Approximate Numbers
rel: Baseline scheme of the SoK.
note: De facto scheme for private LLM inference. Native SIMD over N/2 slots, but non-linear functions need polynomial approximation.

name: RNS-CKKS (full RNS variant)
title: A Full RNS Variant of Approximate Homomorphic Encryption
rel: The form of CKKS implemented in every modern library.
note: Removes multi-precision arithmetic by using a chain of word-sized primes. Enables GPU/ASIC acceleration.

name: Conjugate-invariant CKKS
title: Approximate Homomorphic Encryption over the Conjugate-invariant Ring
rel: Real-only variant that doubles usable real slots.
note: Packs N real values instead of N/2 complex ones. Bootstrapping is more expensive, so it is rarely used.

name: Reduced-error CKKS (FLEXIBLEAUTO)
title: Approximate Homomorphic Encryption with Reduced Approximation Error
rel: Default precision-management mode in OpenFHE.
note: Removes rescaling error from prime approximation. Gains several bits of precision at the same parameters.

name: IND-CPA-D attack on CKKS
title: On the Security of Homomorphic Encryption on Approximate Numbers
rel: Shows CKKS decryptions leak the secret key if shared.
note: Motivates the SoK's assumption that the client never shares decrypted outputs with the server.

name: IND-CPA-D secure CKKS (noise flooding / DP)
title: Securing Approximate Homomorphic Encryption Using Differential Privacy
rel: Hardened CKKS decryption for threshold or shared-output settings.
note: Implemented as NOISE_FLOODING_DECRYPT in OpenFHE. Costs some precision.

name: Multi-key CKKS
title: Efficient Multi-Key Homomorphic Encryption with Packed Ciphertexts with Application to Oblivious Neural Network Inference
rel: Lets client and model owner encrypt under different keys.
note: Enables protecting both inputs and weights. Ciphertext size grows with the number of parties.

name: Threshold / multiparty CKKS (MHE)
title: Multiparty Homomorphic Encryption from Ring-Learning-with-Errors
rel: Distributes the CKKS secret key across parties.
note: Used in Lattigo and OpenFHE for federated and collaborative analytics. Fits double-blind model and data privacy.

name: Bit-CKKS / bootstrapping bits with CKKS
title: Bootstrapping Bits with CKKS
arith: Bits and small integers via CKKS
rel: Turns CKKS into a fast boolean or integer FHE engine.
note: Faster amortized bit bootstrapping than TFHE/FHEW for large batches. Bridges approximate and exact worlds.

name: BLEACH (discrete CKKS)
title: BLEACH: Cleaning Errors in Discrete Computations over CKKS
rel: Runs exact integer/boolean logic inside CKKS.
note: Periodically cleans CKKS noise with polynomial maps. Avoids scheme switching.

name: General functional bootstrapping in CKKS
title: General Functional Bootstrapping using CKKS
rel: Evaluates LUTs during CKKS bootstrapping, like TFHE PBS.
note: The SoK lists it as a robustness direction for piecewise non-linear approximation in LLMs.

name: Gentry-Lee matrix FHE (GL scheme)
title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption for Matrix Arithmetic
rel: Same arithmetic as CKKS but natively on matrices.
note: Removes most rotations and rotation keys in linear algebra. The SoK expects its CKKS recommendations to transfer directly. 2026 follow-ups now cover GL bootstrapping, key size and a first GPU Transformer framework (Terrazzo).

name: First CKKS bootstrapping
title: Bootstrapping for Approximate Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Makes CKKS fully homomorphic.
note: Introduced CoeffToSlot, EvalMod and SlotToCoeff. Every LLM framework relies on its descendants.

name: Improved CKKS bootstrapping (Chen-Chillotti-Song)
title: Improved Bootstrapping for Approximate Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Faster linear transforms and modular reduction.
note: Basis of Microsoft SEAL-era bootstrapping implementations.

name: Non-sparse-key bootstrapping (Bossuat et al.)
title: Efficient Bootstrapping for Approximate Homomorphic Encryption with Non-Sparse Keys
rel: Secure, precise bootstrapping implemented in Lattigo.
note: Removes the sparse-key assumption that weakened security.

name: High-precision bootstrapping (minimax + inverse sine)
title: High-Precision Bootstrapping of RNS-CKKS Homomorphic Encryption Using Optimal Minimax Polynomial Approximation and Inverse Sine Function
rel: Higher bootstrapping precision.
note: Optimal minimax EvalMod approximations, important for deep LLM circuits.

name: META-BTS
title: META-BTS: Bootstrapping Precision Beyond the Limit
rel: Iterative bootstrapping that doubles precision.
note: Trades extra bootstrapping for precision. Useful when deep models accumulate error.

name: Hybrid key switching
title: Better Bootstrapping for Approximate Homomorphic Encryption
rel: The key-switching method used in most libraries.
note: Balances key size and noise. Key switching dominates rotation and bootstrapping cost.

name: KLSS key switching
title: Accelerating HE Operations from Key Decomposition Technique
rel: Asymptotically faster key switching for large parameters.
note: Reduces NTT count in key switching. Relevant to rotation-heavy linear layers.

name: Fused plaintext-ciphertext matmul and bootstrapping
title: Plaintext-Ciphertext Matrix Multiplication and FHE Bootstrapping: Fast and Fused
rel: Folds matrix multiplication into bootstrapping transforms.
note: Related to the operation fusion used by SecretVoice in the SoK.

name: Grafting (CKKS modulus engineering)
title: Grafting: Decoupled Scale Factors and Modulus in RNS-CKKS
rel: Decouples scale factors from RNS primes.
note: Uses word-sized primes with arbitrary scale. Reduces wasted modulus and speeds GPU implementations.

name: SHIP bootstrapping
title: SHIP: A Shallow and Highly Parallelizable CKKS Bootstrapping Algorithm
rel: Very shallow bootstrapping consuming few levels.
note: SoK notes its evaluation keys are larger than classical bootstrapping, so it needs refinement for LLMs.

name: PaCo bootstrapping
title: PaCo: Bootstrapping for CKKS via Partial CoeffToSlot
rel: Small-key bootstrapping (about 0.25 GB keys).
note: SoK highlights it as appealing for LLM inference because key memory is a key bottleneck.

name: Large-interval evaluation
title: Efficient Homomorphic Evaluation on Large Intervals
rel: Extends approximation domains for non-linear functions.
note: SoK cites it for robustness when encrypted activations fall outside the fitted interval.

name: Fast homomorphic Softmax
title: Fast and Accurate Homomorphic Softmax Evaluation
rel: Normalize-and-square Softmax used by SplitPrompt and THOR.
note: SoK's recommended model-preserving Softmax algorithm.

name: Gentry's FHE
title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices
rel: First FHE construction, ancestor of all schemes.
note: Introduced bootstrapping. Impractical today but defines the paradigm.

name: Paillier (partially HE)
title: Public-Key Cryptosystems Based on Composite Degree Residuosity Classes
rel: Supports only addition, no multiplication of ciphertexts.
note: Used in early PPML and federated aggregation. Cannot evaluate Transformers alone.

name: BGV
title: (Leveled) Fully Homomorphic Encryption without Bootstrapping
rel: Exact counterpart of CKKS with plaintext modulus p.
note: Exact arithmetic suits quantized integer LLMs. Non-linear functions and bootstrapping are costlier than in CKKS.

name: BFV
title: Somewhat Practical Fully Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Exact scheme widely used for the linear layers of hybrid protocols.
note: Basis of Cheetah, BOLT, BumbleBee and Nimbus linear layers. No native approximate arithmetic.

name: Brakerski scale-invariant FHE
title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption without Modulus Switching from Classical GapSVP
rel: Theoretical basis of BFV.
note: Removes modulus switching through scale invariance.

name: Revisited BGV/BFV for finite fields
title: Revisiting Homomorphic Encryption Schemes for Finite Fields
rel: Modern BGV/BFV variants implemented in OpenFHE.
note: Lower noise and faster RNS BFV/BGV multiplication.

name: GSW
title: Homomorphic Encryption from Learning with Errors: Conceptually-Simpler, Asymptotically-Faster, Attribute-Based
rel: Basis of FHEW/TFHE blind rotation.
note: Slow noise growth for multiplication by bits. Used as the accumulator in modern bootstrapping.

name: FHEW
title: FHEW: Bootstrapping Homomorphic Encryption in Less Than a Second
rel: Fast per-gate bootstrapping with no SIMD.
note: Exact LUT evaluation of arbitrary functions. Available in OpenFHE, including scheme switching with CKKS.

name: TFHE (CGGI)
title: TFHE: Fast Fully Homomorphic Encryption over the Torus
rel: Exact LUT evaluation of any non-linearity; no approximation error.
note: Main CKKS alternative for non-linear functions. Lacks CKKS-style SIMD, so large matrix products are slow.

name: TFHE programmable bootstrapping for DNNs
title: Programmable Bootstrapping Enables Efficient Homomorphic Inference of Deep Neural Networks
rel: Evaluates activations exactly with lookup tables.
note: Basis of Zama Concrete ML, which supports quantized LLM fragments such as GPT-2 attention heads.

name: TFHE floating point
title: TFHE Gets Real: An Efficient and Flexible Homomorphic Floating-Point Arithmetic
rel: True floating point instead of CKKS fixed point.
note: SoK cites it as evidence that FHE floating point is now feasible but costly.

name: FINAL (NTRU + LWE)
title: FINAL: Faster FHE Instantiated with NTRU and LWE
rel: NTRU alternative to TFHE gate bootstrapping.
note: Smaller keys and faster bootstrapping than TFHE at the time, with NTRU security caveats.

name: High-precision integer HE (CLPX)
title: High-Precision Arithmetic in Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Exact alternative to approximate CKKS for real numbers.
note: Encodes large integers and fixed-point values exactly. Superseded by CKKS for ML.

name: CHIMERA (scheme switching)
title: CHIMERA: Combining Ring-LWE-based Fully Homomorphic Encryption Schemes
rel: Uses CKKS for linear parts and TFHE for non-linear parts.
note: First framework for switching between ring-LWE schemes.

name: PEGASUS (CKKS + FHEW switching)
title: PEGASUS: Bridging Polynomial and Non-polynomial Evaluations in Homomorphic Encryption
rel: CKKS for SIMD linear algebra, FHEW LUTs for exact non-linearities.
note: Scheme switching avoids high-degree polynomials but switching cost is high. OpenFHE implements a variant.

name: Gazelle
title: GAZELLE: A Low Latency Framework for Secure Neural Network Inference
rel: Uses HE only for linear layers and garbled circuits for non-linear ones.
note: Template for most hybrid protocols. Requires many communication rounds.

name: Delphi
title: Delphi: A Cryptographic Inference Service for Neural Networks
rel: Moves HE to an offline preprocessing phase.
note: Fast online phase. Also co-designs activations with polynomial approximation.

name: CrypTFlow2
authors: Rathee, Rathee, Kumar, Chandran, Gupta, Rastogi, Sharma
title: CrypTFlow2: Practical 2-Party Secure Inference
rel: Exact 2PC comparison and truncation protocols.
note: Part of Microsoft EzPC. Basis for SIRNN and later LLM protocols.

name: Cheetah
title: Cheetah: Lean and Fast Secure Two-Party Deep Neural Network Inference
rel: Coefficient-encoded HE matmul without rotations plus OT non-linearities.
note: Basis of Iron, BOLT and BumbleBee.

name: THE-X
title: THE-X: Privacy-Preserving Transformer Inference with Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Early HE Transformer that offloads non-linear steps to the client.
note: Replaces Softmax/GELU and returns some intermediate values to the client, which leaks information.

name: Iron
authors: Hao, Li, Chen, Xing, Xu, Zhang
title: Iron: Private Inference on Transformers
rel: First efficient 2PC Transformer with HE matmul.
note: Model-preserving but gigabytes of communication per inference.

name: MPCFormer
title: MPCFormer: Fast, Performant and Private Transformer Inference with MPC
rel: Replaces Softmax/GELU with quadratic forms and distills.
note: Model-modifying, like the SoK's N-MOD class but for MPC.

name: PUMA
authors: Dong, Lu, Zheng, Wu et al.
title: PUMA: Secure Inference of LLaMA-7B in Five Minutes
rel: Model-preserving 3PC; first private LLaMA-7B inference.
note: About five minutes per token for LLaMA-7B. Needs three non-colluding servers.

name: CipherGPT
title: CipherGPT: Secure Two-Party GPT Inference
rel: First 2PC GPT generation framework.
note: Model-preserving but heavy communication, about 25 GB per token.

name: SIGMA
title: SIGMA: Secure GPT Inference with Function Secret Sharing
rel: GPU-accelerated FSS with a trusted dealer for preprocessing.
note: Seconds to tens of seconds per token for 13B models. Requires offline correlated randomness.

name: BOLT
title: BOLT: Privacy-Preserving, Accurate and Efficient Inference for Transformers
rel: Hybrid with compact HE packing and word elimination.
note: About 10x less communication than Iron. Still interactive.

name: BumbleBee
authors: Lu, Huang, Gu, Li et al.
title: BumbleBee: Secure Two-party Inference Framework for Large Transformers
rel: Hybrid 2PC with efficient HE matmul and accurate activations.
note: Runs LLaMA-7B in about 14 minutes per token. Model-preserving.

name: Nimbus
authors: Li, Yang, Tan, Lu et al.
title: Nimbus: Secure and Efficient Two-Party Inference for Transformers
rel: Client-side outer-product HE encoding for linear layers.
note: Uses low-degree piecewise polynomials for non-linear layers.

name: SecFormer
authors: Luo, Zhang, Zhang, Zhang et al.
title: SecFormer: Fast and Accurate Privacy-Preserving Inference for Transformer Models via SMPC
rel: Fourier-series GELU and Goldschmidt LayerNorm.
note: Balances distillation and model fidelity.

name: Ditto
authors: Wu, Fang, Zheng, Ma et al.
title: Ditto: Quantization-aware Secure Inference of Transformers upon MPC
rel: Quantization-aware MPC with type conversion.
note: Speeds MPC by lowering bit-widths, a direction not yet explored in CKKS.

name: MPC-minimized secure LLM inference (Marill)
authors: Rathee, Li, Stoica, Zhang et al.
title: MPC-Minimized Secure LLM Inference
rel: Fine-tunes LLMs so fewer layers need MPC.
note: Model-modifying. Combines public pre-trained layers with private ones.

name: Centaur
authors: Luo, Chen, Zhang, Liu et al.
title: Centaur: Bridging the Impossible Trinity of Privacy, Efficiency, and Performance in Privacy-Preserving Transformer Inference
rel: Permutes weights so non-linear steps run in plaintext.
note: Weaker privacy than full cryptography but much faster.

name: CrypTen
title: CrypTen: Secure Multi-Party Computation Meets Machine Learning
rel: PyTorch-native MPC framework.
note: Used as the backend of MPCFormer and SecFormer. Supports GPUs.

name: SecretFlow-SPU
title: SecretFlow-SPU: A Performant and User-Friendly Framework for Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning
rel: JAX-to-MPC compiler used by PUMA, BumbleBee, Ditto, Nimbus.
note: Ant Group open-source stack. Comparable role to OpenFHE for the MPC world.

name: MP-SPDZ
title: MP-SPDZ: A Versatile Framework for Multi-Party Computation
rel: Benchmark framework for many MPC protocols, including malicious security.
note: Useful when a stronger threat model than semi-honest is needed.

group: 6. Trusted hardware, statistical and integrity-only alternatives
name: NVIDIA Confidential Computing (H100/Blackwell)
title: NVIDIA Confidential Computing
rel: Near-cleartext speed with trust in hardware vendor.
note: Low single-digit overhead in many LLM workloads, but vulnerable to side channels and requires attestation trust.

group: 6. Trusted hardware, statistical and integrity-only alternatives
name: Confidential computing on H100: benchmark
authors: Zhu, Yin, Deng, Almeida et al.
title: Confidential Computing on NVIDIA Hopper GPUs: A Performance Benchmark Study
rel: Quantifies TEE overhead for LLM inference.
note: Reports under 7% overhead for most LLM queries, versus about 10^4x for CKKS.

group: 6. Trusted hardware, statistical and integrity-only alternatives
name: Apple Private Cloud Compute
title: Private Cloud Compute: A new frontier for AI privacy in the cloud
rel: Production private LLM serving based on hardware trust and transparency logs.
note: No cryptographic guarantee against a compromised operator with hardware access.

group: 6. Trusted hardware, statistical and integrity-only alternatives
name: Intel TDX / AMD SEV-SNP
title: Confidential VMs (Intel TDX, AMD SEV-SNP)
rel: CPU-side TEE often paired with GPU TEEs.
note: Lower throughput than GPU TEE. Known side-channel history.

group: 6. Trusted hardware, statistical and integrity-only alternatives
name: Slalom
title: Slalom: Fast, Verifiable and Private Execution of Neural Networks in Trusted Hardware
family: SGX TEE + outsourced GPU linear layers
rel: Hybrid TEE plus untrusted GPU with blinding.
note: Template for TEE-GPU split designs.

group: 6. Trusted hardware, statistical and integrity-only alternatives
name: Split-N-Denoise (SnD)
title: Split-and-Denoise: Protect Large Language Model Inference with Local Differential Privacy
family: Local DP on embeddings + client denoiser
rel: Formal DP but only statistical privacy.
note: Orders of magnitude cheaper than CKKS, but leaks information within the privacy budget.

group: 6. Trusted hardware, statistical and integrity-only alternatives
name: InferDPT
authors: Tong, Chen, Zhang, Qi et al.
title: InferDPT: Privacy-Preserving Inference for Closed-box Large Language Model
rel: Works with closed APIs without server cooperation.
note: Utility drops at strong privacy levels. No cryptographic protection.

group: 6. Trusted hardware, statistical and integrity-only alternatives
name: PrivateLoRA
authors: Wang, Lin, Zeng, Zhang et al.
title: PrivateLoRA for Efficient Privacy Preserving LLM
rel: Keeps private low-rank layers on device.
note: Activations are exposed to the cloud, so privacy is heuristic.

group: 6. Trusted hardware, statistical and integrity-only alternatives
name: zkLLM
title: zkLLM: Zero Knowledge Proofs for Large Language Models
rel: Proves correct inference; does not hide the user's prompt from the server.
note: Complements CKKS: integrity rather than input confidentiality.

group: 6. Trusted hardware, statistical and integrity-only alternatives
name: EZKL
title: EZKL: zkSNARKs for ONNX models
rel: Verifiable ML inference toolkit.
note: Proof generation is slow for large models.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: OpenFHE
authors: Al Badawi, Bates, Bergamaschi et al.
title: OpenFHE: Open-Source Fully Homomorphic Encryption Library
family: CKKS, BGV, BFV, FHEW, TFHE, scheme switching, threshold
scale: Used by RL, PRITRAN, TRICYCLE, POLARIS, ELLMO, ENSI
rel: Most complete open CKKS library; successor of PALISADE.
note: BSD-2 license. CPU-only core, with GPU back-ends from CEP and FIDESlib.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: Microsoft SEAL
title: Simple Encrypted Arithmetic Library - SEAL
scale: Used by NEXUS, MOAI, EUSTON, STIP, SecretVoice
rel: Popular CKKS library without built-in CKKS bootstrapping.
note: MIT license. Frameworks pair it with Phantom on GPU.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: Lattigo
title: Lattigo: A Multiparty Homomorphic Encryption Library in Go
rel: Go library with strong bootstrapping and multiparty support.
note: Apache-2.0. CPU only.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: HEaaN / HEaaN2
title: HEaaN library
rel: Reference CKKS implementation by the CKKS authors with GPU support.
note: Free for non-commercial use. Closed source.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: HElib
title: Algorithms in HElib
rel: First major HE library; BGV focus.
note: Apache-2.0. Maintenance mode.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: IBM HELayers
title: HeLayers: A Tile Tensors Framework for Large Neural Networks on Encrypted Data
rel: Tile-tensor packing abstraction for neural networks.
note: Free community edition. Not open source.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: Phantom
title: Phantom: A CUDA-Accelerated Word-Wise Homomorphic Encryption Library
scale: Used by NEXUS, MOAI, EUSTON, STIP, ENSI, CACHEMIR
rel: Open GPU CKKS library used by most SoK GPU frameworks.
note: GPL-3.0. Bootstrapping added by downstream frameworks.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: FIDESlib
authors: Agulló-Domingo, Vera-López, Guzelhan, Daksha et al.
title: FIDESlib: A Fully-Fledged Open-Source FHE Library for Efficient CKKS on GPUs
rel: OpenFHE-compatible GPU CKKS server library.
note: Full GPU bootstrapping. Interoperates with OpenFHE client keys.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: Liberate.FHE
title: Liberate.FHE: A New FHE Library for Bridging the Gap between Theory and Practice
rel: GPU CKKS library in Python.
note: SoK notes it is deprecated.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: Cheddar
title: Cheddar: A Swift Fully Homomorphic Encryption Library Designed for GPU Architectures
rel: Among the fastest reported GPU CKKS bootstrapping implementations.
note: Uses 32-bit word arithmetic. Code availability limited.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: 100x faster GPU bootstrapping
title: Over 100x Faster Bootstrapping in Fully Homomorphic Encryption through Memory-centric Optimization with GPUs
rel: Showed CKKS bootstrapping is memory-bound on GPUs.
note: Kernel fusion ideas reused by Phantom, Cheddar and FIDESlib.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: TFHE-rs
title: TFHE-rs: Pure Rust implementation of TFHE
rel: Leading TFHE implementation with GPU support.
note: BSD-3-Clause-Clear, free for non-commercial use.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: Concrete ML
title: Concrete ML: Privacy-Preserving ML with FHE
rel: Compiles quantized scikit-learn and PyTorch models to TFHE.
note: Has LLM examples such as GPT-2 attention and LoRA fine-tuning. Practical mainly for small models.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: Orion
title: Orion: A Fully Homomorphic Encryption Framework for Deep Learning
rel: PyTorch-to-CKKS compiler with automatic bootstrapping placement.
note: Shortest-path bootstrapping placement reused by CACHEMIR.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: HEIR
title: HEIR: Homomorphic Encryption Intermediate Representation
family: CKKS, BGV, BFV, CGGI (via OpenFHE, Lattigo, TFHE-rs)
rel: MLIR-based FHE compiler targeting multiple libraries and accelerators.
note: Apache-2.0. Aims to become standard FHE compiler infrastructure.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: DaCapo
title: DaCapo: Automatic Bootstrapping Management for Efficient Fully Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Automatic bootstrapping placement for CKKS programs.
note: SoK notes optimal bootstrapping placement is NP-complete in general.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: Fhelipe
title: A Tensor Compiler with Automatic Data Packing for Simple and Efficient Fully Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Automatic packing and bootstrapping for tensor programs.
note: Simpler than hand-tuned packing with competitive performance.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: EVA / CHET
authors: Dathathri, Kostova, Saarikivi, Dai, Laine, Musuvathi
title: EVA: An Encrypted Vector Arithmetic Language and Compiler for Efficient Homomorphic Computation
rel: Early CKKS compiler with automatic rescaling.
note: Archived but influential.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: TenSEAL
title: TenSEAL: A Library for Encrypted Tensor Operations Using Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Easy Python tensor API over SEAL.
note: Good for teaching and prototypes. No bootstrapping.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: HEonGPU
title: HEonGPU: a GPU-based Fully Homomorphic Encryption Library 1.0
rel: Open GPU library including CKKS bootstrapping.
note: Apache-2.0. Multi-stream GPU execution.

group: 7. FHE libraries, GPU back-ends and compilers
name: TensorFHE
authors: Fan, Wang, Xu, Hou et al.
title: TensorFHE: Achieving Practical Computation on Encrypted Data Using GPGPU
rel: Uses GPU tensor cores for NTT.
note: Shows AI accelerators can be repurposed for FHE.

name: F1
title: F1: A Fast and Programmable Accelerator for Fully Homomorphic Encryption
rel: First programmable FHE ASIC design.
note: Projected thousands of times faster than CPU. Supports only shallow bootstrapping.

name: CraterLake
title: CraterLake: A Hardware Accelerator for Efficient Unbounded Computation on Encrypted Data
rel: Supports deep CKKS with bootstrapping.
note: Targets unbounded-depth workloads like deep networks.

name: BTS
authors: Kim, Kim, Kim, Jung et al.
title: BTS: An Accelerator for Bootstrappable Fully Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Accelerator designed around CKKS bootstrapping.
note: Memory bandwidth centered design.

name: ARK
authors: Kim, Lee, Kim, Sohn et al.
title: ARK: Fully Homomorphic Encryption Accelerator with Runtime Data Generation and Inter-Operation Key Reuse
rel: Generates data on the fly to reduce memory traffic.
note: Addresses the memory wall that the SoK identifies for LLMs.

name: SHARP
title: SHARP: A Short-Word Hierarchical Accelerator for Robust and Practical Fully Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Uses 36-bit words for smaller area and power.
note: Shows word-size choice matters for CKKS accelerators.

name: Trebuchet
authors: Cousins, Polyakov, Al Badawi et al.
title: TREBUCHET: Fully Homomorphic Encryption Accelerator for Deep Computation
rel: DARPA DPRIVE accelerator for deep computation.
note: Cited by the SoK as evidence for four to five orders of magnitude speedup from custom chips.

name: BASALISC
authors: Geelen, Van Beirendonck, Pereira et al.
title: BASALISC: Programmable Hardware Accelerator for BGV Fully Homomorphic Encryption
rel: BGV accelerator (DARPA DPRIVE).
note: Exact-arithmetic counterpart to CKKS accelerators.

name: Intel HERACLES
title: HERACLES: 8192-way SIMD Programmable Scalable Fully-Homomorphic Encryption SoC
rel: Intel's fabricated FHE SoC.
note: One of the first silicon FHE accelerators.

group: 1. Newer CKKS / FHE LLM frameworks (2026, not in the SoK)
name: Odin
title: An Open-Source End-to-End FHE Implementation for Privacy-Preserving Llama 3 8B Inference
rel: Open-source end-to-end CKKS Llama-3-8B with co-designed packing.
note: Feature-major cross-layer layout and transient per-operator layouts avoid repacking between attention and projections.

group: 1. Newer CKKS / FHE LLM frameworks (2026, not in the SoK)
name: THEMIS
authors: Li, Wang, Li, Tang, Liu, Chen
title: THEMIS: A Co-Designed System for Encrypted Transformer Inference
rel: Plans all stages against one shared CKKS level budget.
note: Bounds depth per stage type and fixes where on the modulus chain each runs. Generalizes coefficient-encoded PCMM.

group: 1. Newer CKKS / FHE LLM frameworks (2026, not in the SoK)
name: ROSETTA
authors: Yu, Zhang, Kong, Ding, Chen, Yu
title: ROSETTA: Efficient and Accurate Privacy-Preserving LLM Decoding via Hybrid CKKS/TFHE Evaluation
rel: Uses CKKS for linear layers and TFHE for decode-stage non-linearities.
note: A scheme-switching alternative to the SoK's pure polynomial-approximation approach.

group: 1. Newer CKKS / FHE LLM frameworks (2026, not in the SoK)
name: Terrazzo (GL scheme on GPU)
title: Terrazzo: Memory-Aware GPU Framework for Private Transformer Inference
rel: First private Transformer inference on the GL matrix scheme, the SoK's flagged successor to CKKS.
note: Co-designs cryptography, algorithms and kernels so GL keys and ciphertexts fit on a commodity GPU.

group: 1. Newer CKKS / FHE LLM frameworks (2026, not in the SoK)
name: Zephyr
title: Zephyr: GPU-Efficient Homomorphic Encryption for Privacy-Preserving Transformer Inference
rel: Redesigns CKKS for 32-bit GPU integer arithmetic.
note: Combines 32-bit words with grafting to remove the 64-bit RNS mismatch on GPUs.

group: 1. Newer CKKS / FHE LLM frameworks (2026, not in the SoK)
name: Error-propagation-aware scale design
title: Error Propagation-Aware Scale Design for Efficient Homomorphic Encryption-Based LLM Inference
rel: Chooses per-operation CKKS scales from measured error propagation.
note: Saves modulus and bootstrapping by using smaller scales where errors do not propagate.

group: 1. Newer CKKS / FHE LLM frameworks (2026, not in the SoK)
name: ATLAS
title: ATLAS: Automated Approximation of Transformers for Efficient Homomorphic Inference in One Hour
rel: Automatically tunes per-layer polynomial degrees and iteration counts.
note: Replaces hand-tuned approximation settings with layer-wise search.

group: 1. Newer CKKS / FHE LLM frameworks (2026, not in the SoK)
name: HEAT
title: HEAT: Faster Fully Homomorphic Inference via Approximations-Weights Co-Adaptation
rel: Fine-tunes weights to tolerate cheaper approximations.
note: Model-modifying (N-MOD style): trades a short training step for fewer bootstraps.

group: 1. Newer CKKS / FHE LLM frameworks (2026, not in the SoK)
name: CGF-Softmax
title: CGF-Softmax: A Cumulant-Based Softmax Reformulation for Efficient Inference under Homomorphic Encryption
rel: Softmax without homomorphic division or max subtraction.
note: Lower depth than normalize-and-square, but it is an approximation of Softmax rather than exact model preservation.

group: 1. Newer CKKS / FHE LLM frameworks (2026, not in the SoK)
name: EncFormer
title: EncFormer: Secure and Efficient Transformer Inference over Encrypted Data
rel: Hybrid that optimizes FHE-to-MPC boundaries with complex CKKS conversion.
note: Cost model chooses where to switch between FHE and MPC to minimize conversions.

name: Discrete CKKS for high-precision bootstrapping
title: Leveraging Discrete CKKS to Bootstrap in High Precision
rel: Reaches about 80+ bit precision needed for noise flooding.
note: Relevant to IND-CPA-D security and threshold CKKS.

name: Fourier-extension functional bootstrapping
authors: Bian, Fu, Shen, Pan, Wang, Guan
title: High-Precision Functional Bootstrapping for CKKS from Fourier Extension
rel: Evaluates smooth functions during bootstrapping with better error bounds.
note: Improves on general CKKS functional bootstrapping for piecewise non-linear layers.

name: Efficient bootstrapping for GL matrix FHE
title: Efficient Bootstrapping in Fully Homomorphic Encryption for Matrix Arithmetic
rel: Bootstrapping for the matrix-native GL scheme.
note: Expresses CoeffToSlot and SlotToCoeff as native matrix products, so key switches per step are a small constant.

name: Low-depth bootstrapping for matrix-native FHE
title: Low-Depth Bootstrapping for Matrix-Native FHE
rel: Reduces bootstrapping depth in GL-style schemes.
note: Same authors as Terrazzo.

name: Trace-Factored BigSwitch (GL keys)
authors: Park, Jeong, Jeong, Oh, Lee, Kim
title: Trace-Factored BigSwitch for Matrix-Friendly FHE
rel: Removes the largest GL evaluation key.
note: Targets the evaluation-key memory bottleneck of matrix-native FHE.

name: SHAFT
title: SHAFT: Secure, Handy, Accurate, and Fast Transformer Inference
rel: Constant-round Softmax and cheaper GELU protocols.
note: Avoids the max extraction that costs logarithmic rounds.

name: CRAfT
authors: Zhao, Yang, Song, Hao, He, Zhang
title: CRAfT: Constant-Round Non-Polynomial Approximation and P2P Network for Secure Transformer Inference
rel: Rotation-free HE packing for many mutually distrusting users.
note: Moves communication to a peer-to-peer network to scale to many users.
